clue.text: Hull supporters knocked out in opening ceremony

definitions.text: Hull supporters knocked out in opening ceremony

parts.words: Hull supporters knocked out in opening ceremony
parts.note: not football fans from the city of Hull but the timber props that hold up a ship's hull on the slipway, which are knocked away when the ship is launched

explanation.surface: Fans of Hull's football team are beaten at the start of some grand event.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a northern English city with a football club, so 'Hull supporters' reads as fans; here it is a ship's hull and the props under it, knocked out at the launching ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipbuilders call the wooden props that steady a vessel on the slipway, removed at its launch, by this name.

clue.text: Piped up to make an entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: tubed means fitted with pipes or sent through a pipe

explanation.surface: A piper strikes up as someone makes their entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piped up' looks like a phrase for speaking, but 'up' turns TUBED backwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear for the first time in public, as a performer does on a first night.

clue.text: Ambitious, like a chief on west coast of India?

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's western coast
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: An eager person is compared to a leader on India's western seaboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the fanciful reading: a chief in Goa would be a Goa head.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person keen to get on is described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Feverish? Bound to be a thermal source!

parts.note: having a fever means being hot
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: A feverish person is sure to give off heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'sure to be', but 'Bound' is a noun meaning a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural source of warm water rising from the ground, heated by the earth.

clue.text: Food and drink not allowed in the ring

parts.note: rabbit is a meat eaten in stews and pies
punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Eating and drinking are banned at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ring' is a boxing ring: a blow to the back of the neck is illegal there.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop to the back of the neck, a foul blow banned in boxing.

clue.text: Doctor's bag?

parts.note: not the case a physician carries but a pouch inside the body, as named in medicine

explanation.surface: A question about what a physician carries their kit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch or cavity within a plant or animal body, in medical and biological language.

clue.text: Nursery bear cuddles cold dog

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold in your arms, so the bear's name wraps around the other letter

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear of children's stories
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A child's teddy bear hugs a chilly little dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a dog, especially a pet one.

clue.text: Finest example of quiet nobleman

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A quiet aristocrat is held up as the best of their kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem from an oyster, used figuratively for the best or most prized of a kind.

clue.text: Harmonium playing as instrument of thought

parts.note: a harmonium is a small reed organ
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A harmonium being played serves as a tool for thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristotle's works on logic were collected under this title, meaning 'instrument' in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of logic or reasoning, used as a tool for thinking, as in Aristotle's logical works.

clue.text: Position of one up?

parts.note: not being ahead in a game but the place where a rider sits, as a jockey is said to be up

explanation.surface: A question about where someone is when they are winning.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey riding a horse is said to be 'up', so 'one up' means a mounted rider, not someone leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Seated on a mount, the place of a rider or jockey.

clue.text: Present holder of party donations

parts.note: not a political fund but a tub of bran at a children's party or fete, with wrapped presents hidden in it for a lucky dip

explanation.surface: Someone currently holds the money given to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like 'current' and 'party donations' like political funds; in fact it holds presents donated for a party lucky dip, a British fete game.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip tub filled with bran in which small gifts are buried for children to fish out.

clue.text: One who organizes the selling plate?

definitions.text: One who organizes the selling plate?

parts.words: One who organizes the selling plate?
parts.note: read as a person who fixes the prices when things are sold, someone who names what to pay, while the question mark points to a large flat serving dish

explanation.surface: A question about who is in charge of a plate being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: One who sets the price of goods 'charges' for them, and the same word names a large flat dish, so 'plate' gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat serving dish, and also a person who sets the price of goods.

clue.text: Employ painter to commit funds, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a painter is the rope at a small boat's bow, so using it means mooring the boat
to lock money into an investment so it cannot be used elsewhere

explanation.surface: Hire a decorator to spend some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' suggests a decorator; on a boat it is the mooring rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat with a rope and locking money into an investment are both expressed by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: For such inequality, I can blame fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to causing an unfairness, blaming fashion for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun being blamed but is a verb telling you to rearrange I CAN BLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of balance or proportion is an inequality between two sides.

clue.text: Jeeves, for example, stand-by over cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A butler stands ready to mix drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves is P. G. Wodehouse's famous valet to Bertie Wooster.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal valet who attends to his employer, as Wodehouse's Jeeves does.

clue.text: In cause of '70's war, Commanding Officer died

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: During a conflict in the 1970s an army commander was killed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Cod Wars' were fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland in the 1970s over fishing rights for this fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish whose fishing grounds Britain and Iceland fought over in the 1970s disputes.

clue.text: X-ray extending from one side to the other

definitions.text: extending from one side to the other

parts.note: an X is a cross shape
a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: An X-ray image spreads right across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X-ray' looks like one thing; split it into X, a cross, and ray, a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A transverse beam or girder spans a space from wall to wall.

clue.text: Difficulty with a load of kit-bags, say

parts.note: an impediment is an obstacle or difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to carry a heavy pile of soldiers' bags.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word for baggage, especially an army's equipment carried on the march.

clue.text: All is much changed in variety

indicators.note: changed letters are altered in order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everything is very different in a mixed assortment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like a mix but is variety entertainment, the British theatre of comic and song acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre with comic and song acts, popular in Britain in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

clue.text: Having become aware of Book I, the study of individual development

parts.note: to be on to something is to have found it out
Genesis is the first book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Discovering the first volume of a work about how a person grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the Roman numeral one, so 'Book I' is the first book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological term for the development of a single organism from egg to adult.

clue.text: Receptacle on counter for wrapping material

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
to foil is to thwart or counter

explanation.surface: A box placed on a shop counter for wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a shop counter but is the verb meaning to thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet used to cover food or wrap items.

clue.text: Post from Baroda? Knock!

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone knocks at the door with letters sent from the Indian city of Baroda.
explanation.walkthrough: Baroda is a city in India, and the answer is an Anglo-Indian word, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Indian word for the mail or postal system.

clue.text: Top game is devilish sticky!

parts.note: a juggling toy, a spool spun on a string held between two hand sticks, whose name comes from the Italian for devil

explanation.surface: A complaint that a game is very difficult indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The toy is played with two sticks and its name is from the Italian for 'devil', so 'devilish' and 'sticky' both point at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A juggling game spinning a two-headed top on a string between two hand sticks.

clue.text: Person on beach treating heat burns?

indicators.note: treating suggests working on something, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone on the sand soothes the sunburnt skin on their behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out to get a tan is typically found on the sand by the sea.

clue.text: Sign of heavenly butter

parts.note: a zodiac sign whose emblem is the ram, an animal that butts with its horns, set in the sky

explanation.surface: A token of divine dairy produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the Ram, first of the twelve signs.

clue.text: Scratches part of sentence, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so a word for part of a sentence is said aloud

parts.note: a clause is a group of words within a sentence

explanation.surface: Someone strikes out part of a sentence, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Claws scratch, so to claw is to scratch or tear with nails.

clue.text: State succeeded with summit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in genealogies
a peak is the summit of a mountain

explanation.surface: A country achieved success at a high-level meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation, but it is a verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to say something out loud, to express it.

clue.text: Touching sweetheart with intention

parts.note: the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet is E
a motive is a reason or intention behind an act

explanation.surface: A lover's gesture is moving because of the purpose behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover but means the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring the feelings; emotional in effect, as a moving story is.

clue.text: It may be Cornish or Dutch. Which would you say?

definitions.text: It may be Cornish or Dutch. Which would you say?

parts.words: It may be Cornish or Dutch. Which would you say?
parts.note: a tree whose varieties are named Cornish and Dutch, and a third kind sounds like the word which, the wych

explanation.surface: Someone asks which of two places a thing comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cornish, Dutch and wych kinds are all varieties of this tree, and 'Which would you say?' hints at wych.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous tree with varieties called Cornish, Dutch and wych, many lost to Dutch disease.

clue.text: Seafood needing one hand only?

parts.note: a shellfish whose name is read as if it could be managed single-handed, by one person alone

explanation.surface: A dish of seafood that can be eaten with one hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible sea snail with a single ear-shaped shell, prized as food.

clue.text: You can't get reproductions of these slippers

parts.words: You can't get reproductions of these
parts.note: the hybrid offspring of a donkey and a horse are sterile and cannot breed

explanation.surface: No copies of this style of house shoe are available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproductions' looks like copies but means offspring: the animal of the same name is sterile.
explanation.definitionFit: Backless slip-on shoes, and also sterile hybrid animals, share the same name.

clue.text: Unsteady low market for wrought iron ware

indicators.note: something unsteady wobbles out of place, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A shaky trade at the bottom of the market for ornamental ironwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Things made of shaped iron or other metals, as by a smith.
